item.title: Bhikkhus, as long as beings have not directly known as it actually is, regarding these four elements, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, as long as beings have not directly known as it actually is, regarding these four elements, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, the escape as escape, they do not live with a mind of seclusion, unattached, unrelated, abandoning obstacles, in relation to the heavenly world, the Māra world, the Brahmā world, together with the generations of samaṇas and brahmins, devas and humans.

And, bhikkhus, when beings have directly known as it actually is, regarding these four elements, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, the escape as escape, they live with a mind of seclusion, unattached, unrelated, abandoning obstacles, in relation to the heavenly world, the Māra world, the Brahmā world, together with the generations of samaṇas and brahmins, devas and humans.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 14.33

item.title: Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are deceitful, stubborn, talkative, fraudulent, haughty, and unconcentrated — those bhikkhus are not my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have fallen away from…
item.description:
Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are deceitful, stubborn, talkative, fraudulent, haughty, and unconcentrated — those bhikkhus are not my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have fallen away from this Dhamma and Discipline. And they do not achieve growth, increase, or expansion in this Dhamma and Discipline. And those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are not deceitful, not talkative, wise, not stubborn, well-concentrated — those bhikkhus are indeed my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have not fallen away from this Dhamma and Discipline, and they achieve growth, increase, and expansion in this Dhamma and Discipline.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.26

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these three taints. What three? The taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. Bhikkhus, these are…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these three taints. What three? The taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. Bhikkhus, these are the three taints.

One who has abandoned the taint of sensual desire,
And the taint of ignorance,
Who has destroyed the taint of existence,
Is liberated from all attachments.
Bearing his final body,
He has conquered Māra and his host.

From: Itivuttaka 57

item.title: ( Blessed One ): For one without anger, Whence does anger come? Living tamed, with right livelihood, Liberated, through right knowledge. That one lives thus,…
item.description:
( Blessed One ):
For one without anger,
Whence does anger come?
Living tamed, with right livelihood,
Liberated, through right knowledge.
That one lives thus,
A life of peace.
Those who, when reviled,
Revile in return,
Do evil to themselves,
And also evil to others.
Those who, when reviled,
Do not revile in return,
That person wins a battle,
A victory for both self and other.
That one seeks the benefit
Of both self and other.
And the one who reviled,
Understanding, calms down.
A physician to both,
Healing self and healing other,
People think him a fool,
Because they do not understand the Dhamma.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 7.2
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects: 'If someone were to break up my friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for me.…
item.description:
Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects: 'If someone were to break up my friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for me. But if I were to break up another's friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for that person. This state that is undesirable and unpleasing for me is also undesirable and unpleasing for others. Since this state is undesirable and unpleasing for me, why should I impose it on others?' Reflecting thus, he himself abstains from divisive speech, encourages others to abstain from divisive speech, and speaks in praise of abstaining from divisive speech. Thus, in verbal conduct, he becomes completely pure.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 55.7

item.title: 'A transgression has overcome me, Venerable Sir, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as I am. For while the Blessed One was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma…
item.description:
'A transgression has overcome me, Venerable Sir, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as I am. For while the Blessed One was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma talk connected with the training, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, I felt impatient and displeased, thinking: 'This samaṇa is too meticulous.' Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept my transgression as a transgression, so that I may restrain myself in the future.' - 'Indeed, Kassapogotta, a transgression has overcome you, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as you are. For while I was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma talk connected with the training, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, you felt impatient and displeased, thinking: 'This samaṇa is too meticulous.' And, Kassapogotta, since you see your transgression as a transgression and make amends according to the Dhamma, I accept your confession. This is growth in the Noble One's Discipline, that one sees a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma, and restrains oneself in the future.'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.91

item.title: The brahmin Asurindaka Bhāradvāja heard: 'The brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth under the Blessed One, from home to homelessness.' Angry and displeased,…
item.description:
The brahmin Asurindaka Bhāradvāja heard: 'The brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth under the Blessed One, from home to homelessness.' Angry and displeased, he went to the Blessed One and, having arrived, reviled and abused the Blessed One with rude, harsh words. Hearing this, the Blessed One remained silent. Then the brahmin Asurindaka Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: 'You are defeated, samaṇa! You are defeated, samaṇa!'

( Blessed One ):
'The fool thinks he wins
When he speaks harsh words.
One who knows how to endure
That one truly wins.

Those who, when reviled,
Revile in return,
Do evil to themselves,
And also evil to others.
Those who, when reviled,
Do not revile in return,
That person has won a battle,
A victory for both self and other.

That one seeks the benefit
Of both self and other.
And the one who reviled,
Understanding, calms down.

A physician to both,
Healing self and healing other,
People think him a fool,
Because they do not understand the Dhamma.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 7.3

item.title: 'Damsels in assembly gather, Ghosts come and go, That forest is called the forest of delusion, How can there be an escape?' ( Blessed One…
item.description:
'Damsels in assembly gather,
Ghosts come and go,
That forest is called the forest of delusion,
How can there be an escape?'

( Blessed One ):
'That path is called the straight path,
That direction is called fearless,
The chariot is called noiseless,
Fitted with the Dhamma-wheel.

Conscience is the chariot's leaning-board,
Mindfulness is its canopy,
I say the charioteer
Is the true Dhamma,
And right view itself
Goes quickly ahead.'

Whether a man or a woman,
Both use that chariot.
By means of that chariot,
They go towards Nibbāna.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.46

item.title: The merit of a giver Always increases, He overcomes hatred, Does not store up restraint. A good person abandons All evil, unwholesome deeds, Destroys greed,…
item.description:
The merit of a giver
Always increases,
He overcomes hatred,
Does not store up restraint.

A good person abandons
All evil, unwholesome deeds,
Destroys greed, hatred, delusion.
His mind is liberated, pure.

From: Udāna 8.5

item.title: 'For their whole life, the Arahants have abandoned non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. Today, this…
item.description:
'For their whole life, the Arahants have abandoned non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. Today, this night and this day, I also abandon non-celibacy, live the celibate life, live aloof, abstain from the vulgar practice of sexual intercourse. By this factor, following the example of the Arahants, I will observe the uposatha day.'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.41
